name: tapp
description: The Tapp Agent Skill for iOS, Android, and web, plus Copilot tools and an auto-refreshing iOS simulator preview.

commands.title: Tapp: Forget saved values for an app

languageModelTools.name: tapp_open_ios_app
languageModelTools.userDescription: Build (if needed) and open the iOS app on the simulator
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Open an iOS app on the simulator and return the current screen as a structured accessibility summary. `target` is optional: omit it to auto-detect and build the Xcode project in the workspace (first build can take minutes), or pass a bundle id (com.example.app), a path to a simulator .app build, or a project directory. For a focused request, ALWAYS pass the user's named destination/control/task in `focus`: Tapp locates it from source and follows the shortest observed UI Map route before returning. Starts an interactive session.

target.description: Optional: bundle id, path to .app, or project directory. Omit to auto-detect the workspace's Xcode project.

focus.description: Focused screen/control/task to source-locate and reach before returning, e.g. 'Save storefront settings visible above keyboard'

languageModelTools.name: tapp_ios_focus
languageModelTools.userDescription: Find a named UI surface in source and take the shortest observed route
languageModelTools.modelDescription: FAST PATH for a focused UI task after tapp_open_ios_app. Pass the user's exact requested screen/control/task. Tapp searches the open repository's source, reconciles it with the runtime-observed UI Map, and executes the shortest trusted route in one call. Use this before step-by-step taps; if no observed route exists it returns exact source evidence and does not wander or invent navigation.

query.description: Requested screen, control, or focused UI task

languageModelTools.name: tapp_ios_login
languageModelTools.userDescription: Sign in — prompts you for credentials if the agent doesn't have them
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Sign in to the open iOS app IN ONE CALL: finds the email + password fields, fills both, submits, and verifies — with all keyboard/secure-field handling done internally. ALWAYS use this for login instead of type/tap sequences (iOS wipes secure fields when editing re-begins). `email`/`password` are OPTIONAL: omit them when you don't know the credentials and tapp will prompt the user directly in VS Code — the values go straight to the app and are never shown to you. Requires tapp_open_ios_app first. On failure, the result includes the on-screen error text.

languageModelTools.name: tapp_ios_fill_field
languageModelTools.displayName: Ask the user for a field value
languageModelTools.userDescription: Prompts you for a value and types it into the app
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Fill a field in the open iOS app with a value provided BY THE USER: VS Code prompts them directly, waits for their answer, and types it into the field — the value never passes through you. Use this whenever the app shows a field whose real value only the user knows (verification codes, search terms, personal data, any credential-like input). `id` is the field's accessibility id, label, or placeholder from the tree; `prompt` is what to ask the user; set `secure` for passwords/codes (masked input). Requires tapp_open_ios_app first.

id.description: Field to fill (accessibility id / label / placeholder)

prompt.description: Question shown to the user, e.g. 'Enter the SMS verification code'

languageModelTools.name: tapp_read_ios_screen
languageModelTools.userDescription: Structured accessibility snapshot of the current screen
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Best default for inspecting the iOS app: returns a structured accessibility snapshot of what is actually rendered on the simulator screen (screen title, elements, controls, hittability). Requires an app opened with tapp_open_ios_app. The iOS equivalent of read_page.

languageModelTools.name: tapp_ios_screenshot
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Visual capture of the current iOS simulator screen, for when layout or appearance matters. Returns the screenshot image and refreshes the Tapp simulator panel.

languageModelTools.name: tapp_ios_tap
languageModelTools.userDescription: Tap a control in the open iOS app
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Tap an element in the open iOS app by accessibility id or visible label (case-insensitive contains match as fallback), and get the resulting screen back. Read the previous result's elements before tapping — never tap from memory. Requires tapp_open_ios_app first.

id.description: Accessibility id or visible label of the element to tap

languageModelTools.name: tapp_ios_type
languageModelTools.userDescription: Type text into the focused field
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Type text into the currently focused field of the open iOS app (tap the field first with tapp_ios_tap). Pass `id` to tap a specific field before typing. Requires tapp_open_ios_app first.

id.description: Optional: accessibility id/label of the field to focus first

languageModelTools.name: tapp_explore_ios
languageModelTools.userDescription: Autonomous iOS exploration → findings, coverage, and evidence
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Explore the iOS app like a user with no authored test and return an observation: deterministic/advisory findings, coverage, an evidence page, screenshots, and a full exploration recording. Takes a few minutes. `target` is optional (same resolution as tapp_open_ios_app). Exploration is not a release gate and returns no score or ship verdict. Report inconclusive coverage and the checked/not-checked scope honestly; use the Tapp CI gate for a merge decision.

target.description: Optional: bundle id, .app path, or project dir. Omit to auto-detect.

languageModelTools.name: tapp_build_ios_app
languageModelTools.userDescription: Build the workspace's iOS app for the simulator and install it
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Build the iOS app from the Xcode project/workspace in the given directory (default: the workspace folder; container and scheme auto-detected), install it on the booted simulator, and return the bundle id. Use when the app is not installed yet or after code changes.

projectDir.description: Directory to search for the Xcode project (default: workspace folder)
